developer: Constructor injection through the container; do not `new` services in methods.
Validate in form requests or validators, keep controllers thin, put logic in services or actions.
Use the ORM or query bindings; never concatenate input into SQL.
Escape output in views; do not echo raw user input.
Routes, middleware and policies: a new route needs authorization and a test.
tester: PHPUnit or Pest tests under `tests/` mirror the namespace; use feature tests for routes and unit tests for services.
Use factories and database transactions; flag tests that rely on seeded data order.
Cover validation errors, authorization failures and not-found paths.
security: `unserialize`, `eval`, `include` of a variable path, shell execution functions on input.
Mass assignment (`$guarded`/`$fillable`), missing CSRF, unescaped Blade output (`{!! !!}`).
peer-review: N+1 queries and missing eager loading; migrations that are not reversible.
Facade and container resolution by string can hide callers from the graph.
Breaking changes in response shapes and route names.
auditor: Rules for PHP should mention constructor injection and tests under `tests/` mirroring namespaces.
